requirement:
When authoring evidence for a requirement, its complete fenced declaration MUST
be included in the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`.
rationale:
**Obligation:** when authoring evidence for a requirement, its complete fenced declaration MUST be in the mandatory input set. `requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs` is cited context, so I did not reassess its own obligations.

**Implementation:** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]` carries the `{impl}` reference. It starts `selectors` with `InputSelector::Requirements { requirements: subject_name }`, which is always the first selector. It later resolves every selector through `fn[source_input]`. That function resolves the selector and returns `selector.to_model_input(&resolved)`, so the output is the declaration's fenced text from `:::{req} name` through the closing `:::`. `fn[source_input]` is reached from `prepare`, so it needs no reference of its own.

**Option lines:** the model input leaves out `:impl:` and `:test:` option lines. `md/reference.md` states that "Option lines are not part of the requirement text", and the code treats them as anchors, which `prepare` contributes separately. The input is therefore still the complete declaration, and I did not count this as a gap.

**Tests:**
- `fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` asserts the first mandatory input equals the full declaration, with the opening fence, body and closing fence.
- `fn[unresolvable_earlier_inputs_do_not_block_reassessment]` asserts the mandatory inputs are exactly the full declaration of `requirements.ready`.
- `fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` also carries a `{test}` reference to the subject. It checks for example that the subject is present when it is an example (`requirements.case`).

All three carry `{test}` references to `requirements.authoring_input`.

**Unspecified behavior:** I found none in this subject's scope.
